blurb:
Pacific Buffet is the call when you want a lot of variety without a lot of hassle. It's an all-you-can-eat setup with sushi, tempura, and American fare all in one place, which makes it an easy yes for groups where nobody can agree. Good for a family lunch or a weeknight dinner when you just want to eat without making a ton of decisions.

The sushi is what most people come for, and it's a solid spread for a buffet. The tempura holds up well too. It's not going to replace your favorite sushi spot, but for the price and the variety, it does the job.

Friday and Saturday they stay open a bit later, until 9:30pm, which gives you some flexibility if you're running behind on a weekend night.

blurb:
We took the family here for lunch not too long ago after finding it on a search, and honestly it delivered. Good service, friendly staff, and a casual setup that works whether you're coming in with little kids or just grabbing a quick weekday meal. It's a solid option on Whitlock Ave when you want something low-key and filling.

The food leans on the greasy side, which for some people is exactly the point. A couple of folks in our group thought it was a bit much, but nobody left unhappy, and we've already talked about going back to try a few other things on the menu. Comfort food done without any pretense.

Friday and Saturday nights they're open until 10pm, which makes it an easy pick if you're out late and don't want to think too hard about where to eat.

blurb:
This is my go-to when I want something solid and filling without spending a lot of time or money. Jerusalem Bakery & Grill is the kind of place you walk into not knowing much about and walk out planning your next visit. Good for a quick lunch, a casual weeknight dinner, or grabbing something on the way home when you don't feel like cooking.

The shawarma is what most people order, and for good reason. It's well seasoned and they don't skimp on the portions. The falafel is legit too, not the dry, crumbly kind you get at places that don't actually care. If you're vegetarian, there are solid options here that don't feel like an afterthought.

Over 5,000 reviews at 4.6 stars tells you this isn't a hidden secret anymore, but it still feels like a neighborhood spot. They're open seven days a week, so no planning required.

blurb:
Marietta Square Market is what happens when you can't agree on where to eat. It's a food hall with around twenty different vendors under one roof, so someone can grab tacos while someone else gets a burger and your kid gets something completely different. We end up here a lot on weekends when the whole family is in town and nobody can agree on anything.

Because the vendor lineup rotates and changes, there's usually something new to try each time you go. The consistent thing is the atmosphere. It's lively without being loud, and there's enough space that it doesn't feel like you're on top of everyone else.

Friday and Saturday they stay open until 10pm, which makes it a decent option for a later dinner if you're coming from something on the Square.

blurb:
If you've got a group coming into town or you're just really, really hungry, Rio is the call. It's an all-you-can-eat Brazilian spot, so you're getting a rotating parade of grilled meat, sides, and everything in between. Great for a family dinner where everyone wants something different, or for a weekend meal when you actually have time to sit and eat slowly.

The cheese bread is ridiculous. Order it as soon as you sit down and don't feel bad about ordering more. The feijoada stew shows up on the menu too, which is a thick black bean and pork stew that's the kind of thing you think about later. My wife and I have both gone back for seconds on that one.

They also do breakfast starting at 10am every day, which is not something most people know going in. Worth a look if you want something different for a weekend morning.
